title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 347
paragraphs: The cow is covered with a crimson robe, except for the head and neck, which are visible, overlaid very thickly with gold; and between the horns there is the disc of the sun rendered in gold. The cow is not standing but kneeling, and in size it equals a large living cow. Every year it is carried out of its chamber — at those times, I mean, when the Egyptians beat themselves in mourning for the god whom I will not name in connection with such a matter. At those times, I say, they also carry the cow out into the light of day, for they say that she asked her father Mykerinos, when she was dying, that she might look upon the sun once each year.
